#summary Documentation and instructions

= Documentation =

!AmFast can encode and decode Python objects to AMF3 format.

= Type Map =

== Python -> AS3 ==

|| Python || AS3 ||
|| None || NULL ||
|| True || true ||
|| False || false ||
|| int || int ||
|| long, float || Number ||
|| str, unicode || String ||
|| dict || Object ||
|| list, tuple || Array ||
|| xml.dom.minidom.Document || XML, XMLDocument ||
|| datetime || Date ||

== AS3 -> Python ==

|| AS3 || Python ||
|| NULL || None ||
|| true || True ||
|| false || False ||
|| int || int ||
|| Number || float ||
|| String || unicode ||
|| Object || dict ||
|| Array || list ||
|| XML, XMLDocument || xml.dom.minidom.Document ||
|| Date || datetime || 



= Encoding =

{{{
import amfast.encoder as encoder
byte_string = encoder.encode(value)
}}}

encode(...)
    Description:
    =============
    Encode a Python object in AMF3 format.
    
    Useage:
    ===========
    byte_string = encode(value, **kwargs)
    
    Optional keyword arguments:
    ============================
     * use_array_collections - bool - True to encode lists and tuples as ArrayCollections - Default = False
     * use_object_proxies - bool - True to encode dicts as ObjectProxys - Default = False
     * use_references - bool - True to encode multiply occuring objects as references - Default = True
     * use_legacy_xml - bool - True to encode XML as old XMLDocument instead of E4X - Default = False
     * include_private - bool - True to encode attributes starting with a underscore  - Default = False
     * get_class_def - function - Function that retrieves a ClassDef object used for customizing serialization of objects - Default = amfast.class_def.get_class_def_by_class Custom functions must have the signature: class_def = function(class_), where class_ is the class of the object being encoded and class_def is a ClassDef instance, or None if no ClassDef was found.



= Decoding =

{{{
import amfast.decoder as decoder
py_obj = decoder.decode(byte_string)
}}}

decode(...)
    Description:
    ============
    Decode an AMF3 stream to Python objects.
    
    Useage:
    ===========
    py_obj = decode(value, **kwargs)
    
    Optional keyword arguments:
    ============================
     * use_array_collections - bool - True to decode ArrayCollections to lists. - Default = False
     * use_object_proxies - bool - True to decode ObjectProxies to dicts. - Default = False
     * get_class_def - function - Function that retrieves a ClassDef object used for customizing de-serialization of objects - Default = amfast.class_def.get_class_def_by_alias Custom functions must have the signature: class_def = function(alias), where alias is the class alias of the object being decoded and class_def is a ClassDef instance, or None if no ClassDef was found.


= Custom Object Types =

!AmFast supports user-defined object types.

{{{
from amfast import class_def

# Map a custom class with static attributes
class_def.map_class(MyCustomClass, class_def.ClassDef, 'class.alias', (tuple, of, static, attributes))

# Map a custom class with dynamic attributes
class_def.map_class(MyCustomClass, class_def.DynamicClassDef, 'class.alias', ())

# Map a custom class implementing IExternizeable
# ExternizeableClassDef must be sub-classed, and the
# methods readByteString and writeByteString must be implemented.
class_def.map_class(MyCustomClass, class_def.ExternizeableClassDef, 'class.alias')

# Map a custom class that is also mapped with SQLAlchemy
class_def.map_class(MyCustomClass, class_def.sa_class_def.SaClassDef, 'class.alias')
}}}
